Exception: std::invalid_argument naming the prim and the attribute. function VarsWrittenBy The render vars chain writes. std::vector< std::string_view > ernie::VarsWrittenBy ( std::span< const SensorFilter > chain ) function VarsWrittenBy The render vars a chain with custom filters writes, a custom integrator writing what the built-in it stands for does (Electrons for one into electrons, HdrColor into linear colour). std::vector< std::string_view > ernie::VarsWrittenBy ( std::span< const SensorFilterStep > chain, const SensorFilterRegistry & registry ) Exception: std::invalid_argument as CheckFilterChain . function ViewPosesOf The views a render product draws through cameras ( RenderProductSpec::cameras ), for images of width x height : none for a single camera without ernie:poses , which draws the one view of its own transform; else the camera-to-world pose of every view in a batch that shares the first camera's lens and sensor, one image each: std::vector< glm::dmat4 > ernie::ViewPosesOf ( const Scene & scene, std::span< const Path > cameras, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height, const Tensor * hostPoses=nullptr ) several cameras: each camera's world transform; one camera with ernie:poses ( tokens::kPoses ): each pose in place of the camera's own transform, under its parent's. Exception: std::invalid_argument if a camera is not a Camera prim, cameras of a batch differ in projection or spectral bands, or the poses are not a CPU (views, 4, 4) float array. hostPoses , when given, stands in for one camera's ernie:poses , such as a host copy of poses written as a CUDA array. function ViewWorldsOf The world each of the views views through cameras sees (see ViewPosesOf ): each camera's world for several cameras; for one camera, its ernie:worlds per pose ( tokens::kWorlds ), or else its world for every view. std::vector< std::int32_t > ernie::ViewWorldsOf ( const Scene & scene, std::span< const Path > cameras, std::size_t views, const HostArrayReader & read={} ) Worlds written on a GPU are read through read . Exception: std::invalid_argument if ernie:worlds is not an integer array of one world per view, or is on a GPU without read . function WireframeOf The wireframe mode of the RenderSettings prim settings ( ernie:wireframe ), Off when unset; a bool means Overlay when true. Wireframe ernie::WireframeOf ( const Scene & scene, const Path & settings ) Exception: std::invalid_argument for a token other than those of WireframeToken . function WireframeToken The token naming mode in ernie:wireframe : "off", "overlay" or "hiddenLine". std::string_view ernie::WireframeToken ( Wireframe mode ) function WorldOf The world of the prim at path ( tokens::kWorld ), from it or its nearest ancestor with one; -1, shared by every world, if none has one. std::int32_t ernie::WorldOf ( const Scene & scene, const Path & path ) function XyzToLinearSrgb Linear sRGB (D65 white, IEC 61966-2-1 primaries) from CIE XYZ. glm::dvec3 ernie::XyzToLinearSrgb ( glm::dvec3 xyz ) function operator& inline constexpr Dirty ernie::operator& ( Dirty a, Dirty b ) function operator| inline constexpr Dirty ernie::operator| ( Dirty a, Dirty b ) function operator|= inline constexpr Dirty & ernie::operator|= ( Dirty & a, Dirty b ) The documentation for this class was generated from the following file ernie/scene/base_schemas.h

docs.text: Type Name class AttributeDef One declared attribute of a prim type. struct AttributeMeta How an attribute is described and edited. Declared with designated initializers in this order. struct AttributeTraits <typename T> How the declared C++ type T reads, writes and converts: Read with the fallback (accepting any numeric or vector type an author used, as GetNumber does), Write , and From , a value as T or nullopt when it cannot be one. struct AttributeTraits< Path > <> struct AttributeTraits< Tensor > <> Bulk data: reads the written tensor or null (there is no fallback), writes with Scene::Write . struct AttributeTraits< bool > <> struct AttributeTraits< double > <> struct AttributeTraits< glm::dvec2 > <> struct AttributeTraits< glm::dvec3 > <> struct AttributeTraits< glm::dvec4 > <> struct AttributeTraits< int > <> struct AttributeTraits< std::string > <> struct AttributeTraits< std::vector< Path > > <> struct AttributeTraits< std::vector< float > > <> class AxisShape An implicit shape centred on its origin along one of its axes: a cylinder, cone, capsule or plane. class Boundable What has local bounds: geometry and instancers, with an optional authored extent. class BoundableLight An area light (sphere, rect, disk): a radiant power, or a photometric power or illuminance. struct BrdfModel A reflectance model: shader source plus parameter metadata. struct BrdfParam One scalar parameter of a reflectance model, with what a UI needs to edit it. class BrdfRegistry Reflectance models available to a renderer, keyed by BrdfModel::id . struct CahvoreModel A camera calibrated in JPL's CAHV family of models, as Mars rovers' cameras are (their PDS labels' GEOMETRIC_CAMERA_MODEL, JPL's camera model files): CAHV, a linear (pinhole) model; CAHVOR, with radial distortion about an optical axis; and CAHVORE, with a fish-eye term and an entrance pupil that moves along the optical axis with the field angle, so its rays do not meet at one point. class Camera A camera looking down its -z axis with +y up: UsdGeomCamera's projection, apertures, clipping, exposure and shutter, and Ernie's lens, scan, spectral sampling, sensor and view poses. struct CameraParams A camera's parameters resolved from its Camera prim ( CameraParamsOf ): a physically based pinhole camera for one image, with UsdGeomCamera's pose, projection and exposure attributes, a spectral range, a lens and a sensor. struct CameraView The raster view of a camera for one frame, derived from a CameraParams by CameraParams::RasterView : what the rasterizer's passes need. class Capsule A cylinder with hemispherical caps along its axis. struct Change A prim's changes since a consumer last looked. struct ChangeCursor A consumer's position in a scene's history; see Scene::Changes . class ChunkedFrameImages The images of a frame of a batch of views that do not fit one set of images (such as more views than an image has layers): consecutive chunks of the views, each its own FrameImages . struct ComputeArrayView A Vulkan image seen by a compute API in place, as an opaque array handle (a CUarray for CUDA, a hipArray_t for HIP): read it with that API's texture or surface objects or 2D array copies. class ComputeInterop Zero-copy sharing between a Vulkan device and the compute device behind it (CUDA or HIP), so arrays from compute frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, CuPy, Warp, simulators) reach Ernie's buffers, and Ernie's results reach them, without passing through host memory. class ComputePipeline A compute pipeline over a PipelineLayout . class Cone A capped cone along its axis, its apex at +height / 2. struct Connection The source of a UsdShade connection: a Shader prim and one of its outputs, e.g. "outputs:rgb". class Cube A box centred on its origin, size along each axis. class CubeSphereLod CDLOD terrain over a whole planet: six LodQuadtree height pyramids, one per face of a cube projected onto a sphere of radius Radius() (a quadrilateralized or "cubed" sphere). struct CubeSphereRegion Region of space holding one node of a CubeSphereLod : every direction within angle of axis , between radii inner and outer from the body's centre. class CudaInterop ComputeInterop for the CUDA device behind a Vulkan device. class Cylinder A capped cylinder along its axis. struct DescriptorBinding One binding of a pipeline's push-descriptor set (set 0). struct DescriptorResource What a binding points at when descriptors are pushed. struct DetailSettings Tiling of the detail albedo and normal textures. struct Device class DiskLight A disk in its xy plane emitting along -z. class DistantLight A light at infinity shining along the -z axis of its transform, such as the Sun. struct DomeDirection One of a dome map's regions of about equal energy ( DomeDirectionsOf ), in the map's frame. class DomeLight Light from every direction, optionally from a latitude-longitude map. struct DomeParams An environment light at infinity (UsdLux DomeLight ) resolved for a frame ( DomeParamsOf ): radiance from every direction, the spectrum radiance (W m^-2 sr^-1 nm^-1 per camera band) times a relative RGB map whose cosine-convolved spherical harmonics are sh . struct DomeSun A sun found in a dome's map ( ExtractDomeSun ), in the map's frame. struct DomeSunExtraction The sun of a latitude-longitude dome map ( tokens::kLightTexture layout) and the map without it, for lighting the sun as a shadowed distant light while the dome keeps the rest of the sky. class EditHistory Undo and redo for scene edits made through it: attribute sets and clears, prims defined, and prims removed with their descendants. struct FrameId Where an image sits in the deterministic random streams of sampling.h . class FrameImages The images a backend renders one frame of a render product into, by render var name: what RenderVarOutput reads, whatever the backend. struct FrameParams Per-frame parameters of a render, whatever the backend: the camera, the sun, the other lights, the sensor filters and the frame's place in the random streams. class FrameUploads Host data bound for device buffers, staged for one frame in flight and copied by that frame's own commands ( Record ), so the host can prepare a frame while the device still runs earlier ones that read the same buffers: the copies wait on the device for that earlier work, in queue order, rather than the host waiting for it. struct Frustum Six world-space clip planes of a view-projection matrix, for culling axis-aligned boxes. class Gprim Geometry: drawn in a display colour, or with a bound material. class GpuBuffer A Vulkan buffer with its memory, allocated through VMA. class GpuImage A device-local Vulkan image with a view of all its mips and layers, allocated through VMA. class GpuTimer Times GPU zones ( ERNIE_GPU_ZONE ) for Ernie's profiler ( ernie/util/profiler.h ) with timestamp queries: a zone writes one timestamp where it starts and one where it ends in its command buffer, and Collect hands finished zones to the profiler without waiting for the device, then frees their queries by host reset (Vulkan 1.2's hostQueryReset). struct GpuXform A prim posed on the GPU: its transform ops are rows of GPU arrays, one row per prim of one Scene::Write of many paths, so a renderer composes its local transform per instance from the arrays whole, as a PointInstancer 's: translate, then orient, then scale. class GraphicsPipeline A graphics pipeline for dynamic rendering, with dynamic viewport and scissor and no culling. struct GraphicsPipelineDesc Fixed-function state of a graphics pipeline that draws triangle lists without vertex buffers. class GroundPlane Ernie: an infinite horizontal floor facing +z at a world height, drawn with its material, optionally as a checkerboard. struct IesProfile A luminaire's photometric profile from an IES LM-63 file (type C photometry): its luminous intensity in candela over the vertical angle theta from its nadir (0, straight down its axis) to its zenith (180 degrees) and the horizontal angle phi around the axis. struct Image RGBA image with linear float channels, rows top to bottom. struct ImageDesc Description of a 2D image or 2D image array. class Imageable What every prim has: visibility and the world it is in. struct InstanceData Per-instance arrays of a point instancer, as UsdGeomPointInstancer defines them. class IsdCameraModel What usgscsm's camera models of image support data share, in the body-fixed frame in metres: class IsdFrame A frame camera from its image support data, its geometry as usgscsm's frame model ( UsgsAstroFrameSensorModel ) computes it ( IsdCameraModel ): the whole image is exposed at once, at the ISD's centre time, from one position and orientation. class IsdLineScanner A line scanner (pushbroom camera) from its image support data, its geometry as usgscsm's line scanner model ( UsgsAstroLsSensorModel ) computes it ( IsdCameraModel ): line l is exposed around its time ImageTime(l) , a rate's start time plus its seconds per line times (l - its start line + 0.5), through detector line 0. class IsdPushFrame A push-frame camera (LROC's WAC, MRO's MARCI) from its image support data, its geometry as usgscsm's push-frame model ( UsgsAstroPushFrameSensorModel ) computes it ( IsdCameraModel ): the image is a stack of framelets, each a frame of FrameletLines lines exposed at once. struct IsdRotation A rotation sampled over time between two NAIF frames, as ALE reads it ( ale::Orientations ): quaternions (w, x, y, z, scalar first) of the time-dependent rotation of vectors from the reference frame into the first of timeDependentFrames , and a constant rotation (row-major, applied to vectors after it) on into the first of constantFrames . struct IsdSamples <typename T> States sampled over time: ephemeris times (seconds past J2000, TDB) and a value at each. struct IsdSensor A camera's image support data (ISD) in the Community Sensor Model's JSON form, as ALE (the USGS Abstraction Layer for Ephemerides) writes it from SPICE kernels for planetary cameras such as LRO's NAC and WAC, MRO's CTX and HiRISE: the image's size and timing, the focal plane's map to detector pixels, the optics, and the spacecraft's and the body's states over the image. struct LensModel A lens: its projection, natural vignetting and transmission. struct LensRayTable A lens given as its rays: unit directions in the camera's frame at every step th sensor pixel corner, ( width / step + 1) by ( height / step + 1) of them row by row from the top left, interpolated between. class Light Any light: UsdLux's LightAPI inputs, its spectrum's shape and Ernie's physical spectrum. struct LightParams A light besides the sun, resolved for a frame from its prim ( LightParamsOf ). struct LodPatch One square patch of PatchCells() x PatchCells() grid quads whose vertices are 2^level raster cells apart. class LodQuadtree Quadtree over a heightfield for continuous distance-dependent level of detail (CDLOD). struct LodRange Distances from the LOD eye, in world units, over which one level's vertices morph towards the next coarser level's. struct LrocWacBandSpec One WAC band's published values. struct MappedRenderVar A mapped render var: a tensor for Cpu and Gpu , a compute array for GpuArray . struct Mars2020Hazcam The Hazcams' optics (Maki et al. struct Mars2020Navcam The Mars 2020 rover Perseverance's Navcam pair (Maki et al. 2020, Table 2). struct MastcamZ class Material How a surface reflects light: Ernie's own inputs, or a UsdPreviewSurface its outputs:surface connects to. struct MaterialSettings How a surface reflects light: a material's settings. class Mesh A polygon mesh: points and the faces over them. struct MeshData Triangle mesh geometry in a mesh's own frame. struct NamedCahvore A named camera model in a frame, as camera model files list them. class NonboundableLight A light at infinity (distant, dome), whose photometric brightness is an illuminance. struct NormalEquations <N> Accumulates the normal equations of a linear least-squares fit, row by row. class OffscreenTarget A colour and depth target for headless rendering, with readback of the colour image. class OrbitController Interactive orbit control of a CameraParams around a target point in a z-up world, for inspecting terrain. class Overlay A named layer of debug drawing: lines, shapes, markers and labels in world coordinates, drawn over the images of render products that ask for it ( tokens::kOverlays ), after the sensor filters, so they never reach observations that do not. struct OverlayItem What every overlay item carries besides its geometry. struct OverlaySegment A line segment of width pixels. struct OverlaySprite A rectangle facing the image at a fixed size in pixels, placed by a world point: rect spans (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) pixels from where anchor projects, y down. struct OverlayStyle How overlay items look. struct OverlayTriangle A filled triangle. class Path Absolute path naming a prim in a Scene , as in USD: / is the root and /World/Sun is the child Sun of /World . class PipelineLayout A pipeline layout with one push-descriptor set and an optional push-constant block shared by all stages. class Plane A one-sided rectangle facing along its axis. class PointBased Geometry from an array of points: a mesh or a point cloud. class PointInstancer Instances of its prototypes (the prototypes relationship's targets) at rows of positions, orientations and scales. class Points Points drawn as spheres widths across, coloured by their display colour. class Prim Handle to a prim in a Scene : its path plus the scene, for chained edits. class PrimSet A fixed list of prims to write rows of one tensor to at once ( Scene::Write ), such as a simulation's bodies every step: the scene looks the prims up the first time and keeps them, looking them up again only after prims are removed or for another scene. struct PrimTypeDef A registered prim type: its name ( Scene::Define 's type), its base, and the attributes it declares itself; abstract ones, such as "Light", are bases only. struct ProductFrame A rendered frame of a render product: its render targets and how to reach them. struct PushbroomStrip A pushbroom camera's strip for one frame ( CameraParams::pushbroom ), as its shaders project with it (projection_pushbroom.slang): its rows' poses run from from (the top row's camera position) to to (the bottom row's), turning from fromRotation to toRotation along the great arc. struct RasterView Non-owning view of a north-up grid of float samples with square cells: the form in which Ernie takes heightfields and albedo maps. class RectLight A rectangle in its xy plane emitting along -z. class RenderDelegate A render backend for a Scene , after Hydra's HdRenderDelegate: the rasterizer, and in future ray and path tracers, behind one interface that applications, the GUI viewer and the Python bindings drive without knowing which backend renders. struct RenderPrims The prims a render of scene uses, as every render delegate resolves them: class RenderProduct One image a render writes: its camera (or a batch of cameras), resolution, render vars and sensor filter chain. struct RenderProductOutput The outputs of one render product in a step: its render vars by name. struct RenderProductSpec A render product to draw, resolved from UsdRender prims. class RenderSettings A render's settings: its camera, resolution and products, and the rasterizer's options. class RenderSettingsBase What render settings and products share (UsdRender's RenderSettingsBase ): the camera, the resolution, and what a product sets in place of its settings' (overlays, minimal shading). struct RenderStats What a delegate holds, for statistics panels. class RenderVar An output of a render product, named by its source, optionally with its own sensor chain. class RenderVarOutput One render var of one rendered frame, such as LdrColor , named after UsdRender's RenderVar . class Renderer Ernie's front door for rendering a Scene headless: a GPU and a render backend on it, with no graphics API to set up. struct RendererInfo What a render backend is and does, so applications, settings panels and bindings can adapt. struct RendererOptions Options for creating a Renderer . struct RenderingTarget Attachments of one dynamic-rendering pass. class Sampler An owned VkSampler . struct SamplerDesc Sampler filtering and addressing. class Scene A lightweight, USD-shaped scene for Ernie: a tree of typed prims named by Path , each holding attributes by USD name, plus change tracking for render delegates. class SchemaView Base of the typed views: a handle to one prim of a registered type, read-only when made from a const scene. class Scope A grouping without a transform of its own. class ScopedGpuZone An ERNIE_GPU_ZONE for Ernie's profiler: timestamps around the rest of the scope's commands. struct SensorChannel One channel of a sensor: its quantum efficiency (electrons per photon) over wavelength. struct SensorFilterModel A sensor filter written in Slang, run in the fused sensor kernel like the built-in ones: a struct typeName in module slang implementing IBandFilter (kind Band , domain Spectrum ), IPixelFilter (kind Pixel , on one of the other domains), or for kind Spatial , which reads the pixels around its own, ISpatialBandFilter (domain Spectrum ) or ISpatialPixelFilter (the other domains). struct SensorFilterOutput One output of a sensor filter. struct SensorFilterParam A custom filter's parameter: a float its prim sets as inputs:<name> , or with size above 1 an array of floats ( float name[size] in the filter's Params , such as a curve; sensor.slang's curveAt reads one), which the prim sets as a float array of any length, resampled linearly to size (a single number fills it). class SensorFilterPrim A SensorFilter prim (Ernie), one step of a sensor filter chain: a filter type and its inputs:* parameters. class SensorFilterRegistry Custom sensor filters a renderer can run, by SensorFilterModel::id . struct SensorFilterStep One filter of a product's chain: a SensorFilter prim's ernie:filter:type , a built-in's name or a registered filter's id, with the floats of its inputs:* attributes by name (without "inputs:"). struct SensorModel An image sensor: channels with quantum efficiency curves, full well, noise, gain and ADC. class Shader A node of a material's network, of the type info:id names, its inputs constants or connections ( <input>.connect ) to other shaders' outputs. class ShaderCompiler Compiles Slang modules at run time with the Slang compiler library, so shaders can be composed from built-in and user-supplied modules (such as custom reflectance models). struct ShaderModuleSource One Slang module given as source text. Other modules import it by name . struct ShadowSettings Cascaded shadow map options. struct SigmoidSpectrum A smooth reflectance spectrum in Jakob and Hanika's sigmoid-polynomial form: s(lambda) = 1/2 + x / (2 sqrt(1 + x^2)) with x = c0 t^2 + c1 t + c2 and t the wavelength mapped from 360-830 nm to 0-1. struct SpectralBands A wavelength range split into count bands of equal width, the spectral sampling of one camera. class Spectrum A spectrum tabulated at increasing wavelengths and linearly interpolated between them; constant beyond the first and last samples. class Sphere A sphere centred on its origin. class SphereLight A sphere (or point) light, optionally shaped to a cone around its -z axis. struct Star One star of a StarField , as renders take it: where it is and the black-body spectrum it shines with. struct StarCatalogue A star catalogue as a StarField 's arrays take it: right ascension and declination in degrees, visual magnitude and B-V colour index per star. class StarField Stars from a catalogue as points of light at infinity, behind everything else, each with a black-body spectrum. struct StarFieldParams The stars of a StarField prim ( StarsOf ) are uploaded when they change; each frame takes only where the catalogue's frame lies ( StarFieldParamsOf ). class StepOperation A submitted step: poll or wait for its GPU work, then fetch its outputs. class Swapchain A presentation swapchain for a window surface, with one "rendered" semaphore per image. class Targets Relationship targets given to a setter: one target (a Path or its text), stored as a single Path , or a list of them, stored as a list; reads take either. class Tensor A strided n-dimensional view of typed memory with an optional owner that keeps it alive: Ernie's end of DLPack. class Terrain A north-up heightfield (x east, y north, z up) drawn with its bound material, or, with a planet radius, a whole planet of six cube faces ( CubeSphereLod ). struct TextureReader A texture read through mesh texture coordinates: a UsdUVTexture with the primvar reader and UsdTransform2d feeding it, which is also glTF's textureInfo with KHR_texture_transform and MaterialX's image, texcoord and place2d nodes. struct TimelinePoint A wait for or a signal of a timeline semaphore value in a submission. struct TriangleCorners Where each corner of TriangulateFaces ' triangles comes from: its face and its position in faceVertexIndices , for primvars with uniform and faceVarying interpolation. class Value A scene attribute value: one of the scalar, vector, matrix, token, relationship and small-array types Ernie's schemas use. class Volume A volume (UsdVol); Ernie does not draw volumes yet. class VulkanContext Owns a Vulkan instance, device, graphics and compute queue, and memory allocator. struct VulkanContextOptions Options for VulkanContext::Create . class Xform A transform grouping its children. struct XformOps A prim's local transform as translate, rotate (Euler angles or a quaternion) and scale, the ops of USD's UsdGeomXformCommonAPI.

docs.text: Type Name enum AttributeKind What an attribute holds, from its declared C++ type. enum Axis The axis a primitive is built around, as UsdGeom's axis token. enum BayerPattern The Bayer layouts of the bayer and demosaic filters' pattern . typedef std::pair< glm::vec3, glm::vec3 > Bounds3 Axis-aligned world bounds, low and high corners. enum BufferMemory Where a buffer lives and how the host reaches it. enum CubeFace The faces of a wide camera's views: forward along the camera's -z, then its +x, -x, +y, -y and +z (back). typedef ComputeArrayView CudaArrayView The view of an image CudaInterop::MapImage returns ( array is a CUarray ). enum std::uint32_t Culling How the rasterizer culls what lies outside a view ( ernie:culling ). enum std::uint8_t DType Element types Ernie exchanges. enum std::uint8_t DeviceKind Where a tensor's memory lives: host memory, or the memory of a CUDA or ROCm (HIP) device. enum std::uint32_t Dirty What changed about a prim, as bit flags; see DirtyOf for which attributes set which bit. enum DomeLightMode How dome lights light the scene ( tokens::kDomeLightMode ), as Omniverse RTX's modes. typedef int ExternalHandle Memory or a semaphore exported for another API, such as CUDA: a POSIX file descriptor, or a Win32 NT handle on Windows. enum std::uint8_t FilterDomain What a filter works on (sensor.slang's SensorPixel ): each band's radiance ( Spectrum ), the channels' electrons (after QE), their digital numbers (after ADC), linear sRGB (after CIE) or the sRGB-encoded display colour (after exposure). enum std::uint8_t FilterKind How a sensor filter runs in the fused sensor kernel (sensor.slang): typedef std::function< Tensor (std::string_view attribute, const Tensor &device)> GpuOpReader Copies an op's tensor on a GPU ( attribute 's, a prim's row of an array) to the host. typedef std::function< Tensor (const Path &path, std::string_view attribute, const Tensor &device)> HostArrayReader A host copy of array attribute of path , written as device on a GPU: for the few arrays the CPU plans with, such as worlds. enum ImageEncoding How 8- and 16-bit stored values map to linear values. enum std::uint8_t LensProjection How a lens maps the field angle of a ray to its place in the image. enum std::uint32_t LightType Kinds of LightParams . enum LrocNac LROC's two Narrow Angle Cameras, side by side across the track. enum LrocWacBand The seven bands of LROC's Wide Angle Camera , by Robinson et al. enum MapDevice Where RenderVarOutput::Map delivers an output. enum std::uint8_t MarkerShape The shape of a marker, drawn at a fixed size in pixels. enum Mars2020Hazcams Perseverance's hazard cameras: two stereo pairs on the front of the rover body (looking down past the front wheels) and one on the back. enum MastcamZEye The Mars 2020 rover Perseverance's Mastcam-Z: two zoom cameras whose filter wheels hold the Bayer RGB's near-IR cut-off (filter 0), six narrow bands from 442 to 1022 nm (1 to 6) and a neutral-density solar filter (7), the left camera's bands visible and the right's reaching into the near infrared (Bell et al. enum std::uint32_t MinimalMode Minimal shading ( ernie:minimal:mode ), after RTX Minimal: for throughput, a product draws in one forward pass straight into its outputs, without the spectral shading, sensor filters, sky or dome; lit by the sun (the first distant light) and the ambient fraction. enum MipFilter How MipChain filters each level. enum std::uint32_t Occlusion Whether the rasterizer also culls instances hidden behind others ( ernie:occlusion ), with GPU culling and for views only (not shadow views). enum std::uint8_t OverlayDepth How an overlay item meets the scene's surfaces. typedef std::map< Path , RenderProductOutput > RenderProductSetOutputs Outputs of a step by render product path. enum std::uint8_t RotationOrder The axis order of an Euler-angle rotate op: the rotation about the first letter's axis applies first, about fixed (extrinsic) axes. enum std::uint8_t SensorFilter The built-in sensor filters a render product runs in order on its spectral radiance, as Chrono::Sensor's filter lists; the rasterizer fuses a chain into one kernel ( PlanSensor ), so the vars below are written only when held: enum std::uint32_t ShadowFit What bounds a single view's sun cascades ( ernie:shadows:fit ). enum TextureColorSpace How a texture's stored values map to linear ones (UsdUVTexture's sourceColorSpace). enum TextureWrap How a texture repeats outside [0, 1] along one axis (UsdUVTexture's wrapS and wrapT). enum std::uint32_t Wireframe How the rasterizer draws triangle edges ( ernie:wireframe ). enum std::uint32_t WorldShadowFit What a world's own shadow map covers ( ernie:shadows:worldFit ). enum std::uint32_t WorldShadows Which casters shadow a batch of views of several worlds ( ernie:shadows:worlds ).

docs.text: Spectral quantities for Ernie's spectral rendering: wavelengths in nanometres, spectral irradiance in W m^-2 nm^-1 and spectral radiance in W m^-2 sr^-1 nm^-1. Deterministic random streams shared by every render backend. How every render delegate reads a Scene : which prims a render uses, its render products, and the camera, lights, materials, meshes and instances as plain data, so backends differ only in how they draw. Rays of a lens in the camera's frame, and the cube faces a wide camera's views are rendered on, for fields the single pinhole raster image cannot take (its tangent grows without bound towards 90 degrees off axis). Helpers for authoring and reading the schemas in tokens.h . Scenes described in JSON, the format of Python's ernie.load_scene : The view reads and writes the scene's attributes by their USD names, so it changes nothing about storage or change tracking; unset attributes read as the declared fallback, the one place Ernie keeps it. A schema's header declares its attributes with an X-macro list and its class with ERNIE_SCHEMA_BODY ; its source defines the registry entry with ERNIE_DEFINE_SCHEMA , and prim_type.cpp lists it in the registry. See light_schemas.h . References: * Blender, Cycles' node types and sockets ( NODE_DEFINE , SOCKET_* , NODE_SOCKET_API ), https://projects.blender.org/blender/cycles/src/branch/main/src/graph/node_type.h * Pixar, UsdLux and generated schema classes, https://openusd.org/release/api/usd_lux_page_front.html The top level maps prim paths (absolute, or relative to the root) to prims. A prim is an object: "type" names its type ( Scene::Define ; registered or not). Without one, a new prim is untyped and an existing prim keeps its type and attributes. Keys whose values are objects are its children, by name; the other keys are its attributes, by the Python name of one its type declares ( AttributeDef::pyName , "cell_size") or by USD name ("inputs:intensity"). translate (3 numbers), rotate (3 Euler angles in degrees), rotation_order ("XYZ", ..., "ZYX"), orient (a quaternion as [w, x, y, z], the real part first as USD writes one and as Python's Quat(w, x, y, z) takes it) and scale (one number or 3) set its transform ops ( SetXform ); transform sets xformOp:transform to a 4 x 4 matrix given as 4 rows of 4 numbers (math convention: column vectors, translation in the last column). Values convert as Python's do: booleans, integers (32-bit), other numbers as doubles, strings, arrays of strings, arrays of 2 numbers ( ivec2 when both are integers), 3 or 4 as vectors, other lengths as float arrays, and 4 x 4 nested arrays as matrices. A declared attribute's value is then converted to its type ( AttributeDef::Coerce : a string to a relationship target, say); one declared as a tensor ( points , heights ) takes a possibly nested array as a CPU tensor, int32 for one of whole numbers ( AttributeMeta::integer : indices, counts) and float32 for any other, whatever the numbers look like, written with Scene::Write . A declared 4-vector takes its 4 numbers as doubles, and a declared AttributeMeta::lenient attribute keeps a value its type cannot convert. On any other attribute, nested arrays other than 4 x 4 (such as a per-vertex primvars:displayColor , N rows of 3) are a float32 tensor; on an undeclared one, 4 numbers for an xformOp:orient (or xformOp:orient:<suffix> ) are a quaternion as [w, x, y, z]. Values are checked as Scene::Set checks them ( Validate ). SaveScene writes the format back, so that LoadScene of its text into an empty scene rebuilds the scene: every prim but the viewer's (under tokens::kSessionRoot ), roots by path at the top level and the others nested as children by name, "type" first when typed, then the attributes by USD name in name order (transform ops as xformOp:* and xformOpOrder attributes, not the translate -style keys), then the children in path order. Values are written as LoadScene reads them back: Path s and lists of them as strings, matrices as 4 rows, quaternions as [w, x, y, z], floats in their shortest form that reads back as the same float, and tensors as arrays nested by their shape. Limits: * large tensors make large files (a number per element, a line per row), and NaN or infinite numbers cannot be written (JSON has none); * declared attributes come back as their declared types; undeclared ones as LoadScene reads the JSON: Path s as strings, 2 to 4 numbers as vectors (a float array or a rank-1 tensor of that length among them, and a dvec4 or a quaternion off xformOp:orient as a float vec4 ), other rank-1 arrays as float arrays, nested arrays as float32 tensors (any element type), and a 4 x 4 tensor as a matrix; * declared tensors come back int32 ( AttributeMeta::integer ) or float32 whatever their element type; an empty tensor comes back without its shape and a rank-0 one with shape [1]; * an empty list of strings or paths comes back as an empty float array (declared relationship lists convert it back), and unset ( Value::Empty ) values are left out; * overlays ( Scene::GetOverlay ) are not prims and are not written; * GPU tensors are not copied to the host: SaveScene throws for them. The readers accept any numeric type an author might use for an attribute (an int , float or double number; a vec or dvec vector), since bindings such as Python's produce doubles. The camera's frame is USD's: x right, y up, looking down -z. A cube face is a square pinhole view of 90 degrees (plus a margin) along one of the camera's axes; the sensor follows each pixel's lens ray to the face it leaves through. kernel/film/cube_faces.slang holds the same conventions for the sensor kernel. References: * N. Greene, "Environment Mapping and Other Applications of World Projections", IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications 6(11):21-29, 1986 (cube maps). * Khronos, "Vulkan Specification", 16.5.4 "Cube Map Face Selection" (selection by the largest-magnitude component). Every random decision a renderer makes (sensor noise, and the samples of ray and path tracers) derives from three numbers: a seed the scene authors, a stream naming what is rendered (a render product, StreamOf its path) and the frame number. The same scene, settings and frame then render the same image on any machine, in any order, whatever else renders alongside. Reference: M. Jarzynski and M. Olano, "Hash Functions for GPU Rendering", Journal of Computer Graphics Techniques 9(3):21-38, 2020 (pcg3d).

docs.text: The built-in sensor filters a render product runs in order on its spectral radiance, as Chrono::Sensor's filter lists; the rasterizer fuses a chain into one kernel ( PlanSensor ), so the vars below are written only when held: enum ernie::SensorFilter { Lens, Qe, Noise, Adc, Cie, Exposure }; Lens : resamples the radiance into sensor pixels through the inverse lens distortion, with cos^4 vignetting; writes SpectralRadiance and the geometry vars. Always runs first. Qe : mean electrons per channel (camera equation, quantum efficiency, dark current); writes Electrons. Noise : shot, read, PRNU and DSNU noise on Electrons. Adc : digital numbers from Electrons; writes RawDN. Cie : linear sRGB in cd/m^2 through the CIE observer; writes HdrColor. Exposure : the photographic output, HDR colour times the exposure scale, sRGB-encoded; writes LdrColor.

docs.text: Authors one of LROC's Narrow Angle Cameras as published, onto Camera camera and the readout chain of RenderProduct product . void ernie::AuthorLrocNac ( Scene & scene, const Path & camera, const Path & product, LrocNac which=LrocNac::Left ) The image's geometry (pose along the orbit, focal length, detector line, summing, lens distortion and line time) comes from its ISD ( IsdLineScanner::StripOf , Python's IsdLineScanner.author_strip ); this sets the rest: * The sensor: one panchromatic channel over the 400-760 nm spectral response with the detector's average quantum efficiency through it (> 60%: 0.6, its edges ramped over 10 nm; the paper gives no curve), the gain, detector noise and full well of NAC-L or NAC-R, a 12-bit ADC and the telescope's f-number. * The readout chain, SensorFilter prims under product : qe, noise, adc, readoutTaps (the even and odd pixels' two analog chains, offsets 0 until calibrated) and compandTable (the nominal 12- to 8-bit table, code 0), so RawDN holds the 8-bit numbers the NAC sends. Reference: M. S. Robinson et al., "Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) Instrument Overview", Space Science Reviews 150:81-124, 2010: sections 3.1 and 4.1, Table 2 (focal ratio, gain, detector noise, full well, spectral response, digitisation) and Appendix A (bit-compression tables). Exception: std::invalid_argument if camera is not a Camera or product not a RenderProduct .
docs.title: function AuthorLrocNac

docs.text: Authors one band of LROC's Wide Angle Camera as published, onto Camera camera and the readout chain of RenderProduct product . void ernie::AuthorLrocWac ( Scene & scene, const Path & camera, const Path & product, LrocWacBand band=LrocWacBand::Vis605 ) The image's geometry (each framelet's pose, focal length, lens distortion and exposure) comes from its ISD ( IsdPushFrame::FrameletOf , Python's IsdPushFrame.author_framelet ); this sets the rest: * The sensor: one channel through the band, its passband Table 4's FWHM wide about the effective wavelength (edges ramped over 2 nm about the half maxima, so its area is the FWHM's) at the band's effective quantum efficiency ( LrocWacBandSpec::EffectiveQe ), the lens's transmission 1 (in that efficiency); the KAI-1001's gain, read noise and full well; an 11-bit ADC; the band's optics' f-number. The camera's spectral range is narrowed to the passband, four bands across it. * The readout chain, SensorFilter prims under product : qe, noise and adc, so RawDN holds the 11-bit numbers before the WAC's companding to 8 bits, which the paper gives only as a figure (Fig. 25). Reference: M. S. Robinson et al., "Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) Instrument Overview", Space Science Reviews 150:81-124, 2010: section 3.2, Table 3 (focal ratios, gain, read noise, full well, digitisation, summing) and Table 4 (bandpasses and responsivity). Exception: std::invalid_argument if camera is not a Camera or product not a RenderProduct .

docs.text: Authors one of the Mars 2020 Navcams as published, onto Camera camera and the readout chain of RenderProduct product : void ernie::AuthorMars2020Navcam ( Scene & scene, const Path & camera, const Path & product, BayerPattern pattern=BayerPattern::Rggb, double jpegQuality=85.0 ) The camera: the f-theta lens ( Mars2020Navcam::FisheyeK1 , Ernie's fisheye) of 19.1 mm over the full 32.77 x 24.58 mm frame, f/12, focused at 3.5 m. Render it at 5120 x 3840 for the detector's own 6.4 um pixels; a smaller resolution bins them (as the cameras can downsample), each pixel then wider and collecting more light. The sensor: RGB, the CMV-20000's gain, dark noise and full well, a 12-bit ADC. The paper gives the detector's QE only as 64.5% at 550 nm (monochrome, with microlenses; its table prints "55 nm"), with no colour responses, so the channels keep Ernie's generic RGB curves. The readout chain, SensorFilter prims under product : qe, bayer ( pattern ; the paper does not give the layout), noise, adc and demosaic (Malvar-He-Cutler), so RawDN holds the 12-bit numbers demosaiced; then cie, exposure and jpeg at jpegQuality for the 8-bit colour images the rover sends JPEG-compressed (the paper gives the quality as selectable). Fixed-pattern noise and dark current are not published; add darkCurrent or defectPixels filters to model them. Reference: J. N. Maki et al., "The Mars 2020 Engineering Cameras and Microphone on the Perseverance Rover: A Next-Generation Imaging System for Mars Exploration", Space Science Reviews 216:137, 2020, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11214-020-00765-9: Table 2 and sections on the detector and flight software. Exception: std::invalid_argument if camera is not a Camera or product not a RenderProduct .

docs.text: Authors one Mastcam-Z camera through filter filter as published, onto Camera camera and the readout chain of RenderProduct product : void ernie::AuthorMastcamZ ( Scene & scene, const Path & camera, const Path & product, MastcamZEye eye, int filter, double focalLengthMm=MastcamZ::kShortestFocalMm, BayerPattern pattern=BayerPattern::Rggb ) The camera: a pinhole of focalLengthMm (26 to 110) over the 11.84 x 8.88 mm detector at its f-number ( MastcamZ::FNumberAt ). Filter 0: an RGB sensor whose channels are Gaussians at Table 3's Bayer effective wavelengths and half widths, peaking at the detector's ~40%; the chain qe, bayer ( pattern ; the paper does not give the layout), noise, adc, demosaic. Filters 1 to 7: one channel, the filter's passband (Table 3's 2 x HWHM wide about its effective wavelength, ramped over 2 nm about the half maxima, times 10^-ND for filter 7) on the detector's response, Ernie's generic silicon curve scaled to the ~40% peak (the paper publishes no curve, and the Bayer microfilters' differences in a narrow band are left out); the camera's spectral range narrowed to the passband, four bands across it; the chain qe, noise, adc. The sensor: the KAI-2020CM's gain, read noise and full well for eye , an 11-bit ADC. Scene radiance past 830 nm follows what the scene gives there: materials' RGB albedo holds its 830 nm value, so give materials reflectance spectra for the near-IR bands. Reference: J. F. Bell III et al., "The Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Mast Camera Zoom (Mastcam-Z) Multispectral, Stereoscopic Imaging Investigation", Space Science Reviews 217:24, 2021, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11214-020-00755-x: Tables 3 and 5 and the focal plane section. Exception: std::invalid_argument if camera is not a Camera , product not a RenderProduct , filter outside 0 to 7 or focalLengthMm outside the zoom.

docs.text: Sets lens 's chromatic aberration ( LensModel::chromaticScale , chromaticFocusMm ) for a thin singlet of focal length focalLengthMm at the d line (587.56 nm) in a glass of refractive index nd and Abbe number abbe : the index by Cauchy's dispersion n = A + B / lambda^2 through n_d and n_F - n_C = (n_d - 1) / V_d (the F and C lines at 486.13 and 656.27 nm), the focal length by the lensmaker's equation, f(lambda) = f_d (n_d - 1) / (n(lambda) - 1), whose shift f(lambda) - f_d is the axial colour (f_C - f_F = f_d / V_d, about). void ernie::SetSingletChromatic ( LensModel & lens, double focalLengthMm, double nd, double abbe, double lateral=0.0 ) The lateral colour is lateral times the relative change, the image's scale 1 + lateral (f / f_d - 1): 0 for a stop at the lens, where the chief ray passes undeviated, up to 1 for a distant stop. Tabulated every 10 nm from 300 to 1100 nm. References: * A.-L. Cauchy, "Mémoire sur la dispersion de la lumière", 1836. * E. Hecht, "Optics", 5th ed., Pearson, 2017, sections 6.3.2 (chromatic aberrations) and 6.2 (thick lenses). * SCHOTT, "Optical Glass Datasheets" (n_d and V_d at the d, F and C lines). docs.text: The standard library of sensor filters, written in Slang like custom ones and registered with every renderer, for a SensorFilter prim's ernie:filter:type : std::vector< SensorFilterModel > ernie::StandardSensorFilters () psf (spatial, spectrum): the lens's point-spread, diffraction for the camera's f-number per band (a Gaussian fit to the Airy disc) and a Gaussian blur in pixels; before qe . defocus (spatial, spectrum): thin-lens depth of field from the camera's fStop and focusDistance ; before qe . bayer (pixel, electrons): a Bayer colour filter mosaic, pattern 0 RGGB, 1 BGGR, 2 GRBG, 3 GBRG; best between noise and adc . demosaic (spatial, digital): interpolates the mosaic back, method 0 bilinear or 1 Malvar-He-Cutler; after adc . AOV mosaic : the mosaic it read. blooming (spatial, electrons): charge beyond the full well spilling along columns, antiBlooming the fraction drained; after qe . AOV overflow : the charge beyond the well. whiteBalance (pixel, rgb): red , green and blue gains; after cie . colorMatrix (pixel, rgb): a 3 x 3 colour correction matrix m00 .. m22 ; after cie . compand (pixel, digital): square-root companding from inputBits to outputBits ; after adc . toneCurve (pixel, display): each channel through curve (33 samples over 0 to 1); after exposure . spectralTransmission (band): each band times curve (48 samples, 360 to 830 nm), a measured filter's transmission; before qe and cie . lag (pixel, electrons; temporal): a fraction of each frame's charge read out with the next. temporalAverage (pixel, rgb; temporal): an exponential moving average, alpha the new frame's weight. Each file's header cites its references.

docs.text: Struct ernie::BrdfModel ClassList > ernie > BrdfModel A reflectance model: shader source plus parameter metadata. More... #include <ernie/scene/brdf.h> Public Attributes Type Name std::string description std::string id Stable identifier used in settings, e.g. "hapke". std::string name Display name. std::vector< BrdfParam > params std::vector< std::string > references std::string slang std::string typeName Slang struct implementing IBrdf , e.g. "Hapke". Public Functions Type Name std::vector< float > Defaults () const Default value of every parameter, in order. Detailed Description slang is a Slang module that may import brdf; ( BrdfSlang ) and defines a struct named typeName implementing IBrdf , whose radianceFactor(BrdfInput s, BrdfParams p) returns the radiance factor I/F (pi times the bidirectional reflectance) for unit incident irradiance. Parameter i , in the order of params , is p.get(i) . BrdfInput carries cos(i), cos(e), cos(g), the cosine of the azimuth between the incidence and emission planes, an rgb albedo input whose meaning each model documents, and the variance per axis of surface slopes finer than the renderer resolves (a filtered normal map's), which models with a roughness add to it ( widenedMeanSlope for Hapke-like ones) and others may ignore. A model only defines radianceFactor ; every render backend evaluates and samples it through the generic helpers of the brdf module ( evaluateBrdf , sampleBrdf , brdfPdf ), so a model works unchanged in the rasterizer and in ray and path tracers. CameraView RasterView (double overscan=1.0) const The raster view: the inverse pose, and a projection with the focal length divided by overscan (so with lens distortion it covers the undistorted rays of every sensor pixel), the principal point and the clipping range. CameraView RasterView (const glm::dmat4 & pose, double overscan) const RasterView from camera-to-world pose in place of transform , such as one view of a batch, without copying the camera. void SetVerticalFov (double radians) Sets the vertical aperture so the image spans radians vertically at the focal length. double SubframeTime (int subframe) const The time of sub-frame subframe in frames relative to the frame's: evenly spaced from the top row's opening to the bottom row's closing, the last at shutterClose . int Subframes () const The sub-frames a frame renders: 1 with the shutter closed (open equal to close) and a global shutter, else shutterSamples , at least 2. double VerticalFov () const The vertical field of view in radians. Detailed Description The pose transform maps camera to world coordinates; as in USD the camera looks down its -z axis with +y up. Interactive controls such as OrbitController write it. Focal length and apertures are read in millimetres. The image fits the vertical aperture: pixels are square with a pitch of verticalAperture / height , and the horizontal aperture follows from the image's aspect. Aperture offsets shift the principal point. An orthographic camera follows UsdGeomCamera (and GfCamera): its apertures and their offsets are in tenths of a scene unit, the size of the view in the scene, and it has no focal length; every ray runs along the view direction. Its optics are telecentric, without fall-off off axis or depth of field, and its pixels have the pitch orthographicPixelPitchUm on the sensor. Its lens has no distortion. Distances to the camera are from its image plane. Terrain levels of detail still follow the distance from the camera's position, so place it near what it sees. Radiometry follows the camera equation: a scene radiance L reaches the sensor as irradiance E = L pi t cos^4(theta) / (4 N^2) for an object far away, with transmission t, f-number N and field angle theta; a pixel collects E times its area times the exposure time, converted to photons and electrons per band. The photographic outputs instead scale luminance by USD's linear exposure scale; with a one-channel (monochrome) sensor they are grey, weighting the bands by that channel's quantum efficiency, scaled so a flat spectrum keeps its luminance. docs.text: The pose transform maps camera to world coordinates; as in USD the camera looks down its -z axis with +y up. Interactive controls such as OrbitController write it. Focal length and apertures are read in millimetres. The image fits the vertical aperture: pixels are square with a pitch of verticalAperture / height , and the horizontal aperture follows from the image's aspect. Aperture offsets shift the principal point. An orthographic camera follows UsdGeomCamera (and GfCamera): its apertures and their offsets are in tenths of a scene unit, the size of the view in the scene, and it has no focal length; every ray runs along the view direction. Its optics are telecentric, without fall-off off axis or depth of field, and its pixels have the pitch orthographicPixelPitchUm on the sensor. Its lens has no distortion. Distances to the camera are from its image plane. Terrain levels of detail still follow the distance from the camera's position, so place it near what it sees. Radiometry follows the camera equation: a scene radiance L reaches the sensor as irradiance E = L pi t cos^4(theta) / (4 N^2) for an object far away, with transmission t, f-number N and field angle theta; a pixel collects E times its area times the exposure time, converted to photons and electrons per band. The photographic outputs instead scale luminance by USD's linear exposure scale; with a one-channel (monochrome) sensor they are grey, weighting the bands by that channel's quantum efficiency, scaled so a flat spectrum keeps its luminance. References: * B. K. P. Horn, "Robot Vision", MIT Press, 1986 (the image irradiance equation E = L (pi / 4) (d / f)^2 cos^4(alpha), with N = f / d). * Pixar, "UsdGeomCamera", https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_geom_camera.html

Protected Functions Type Name ComputeInterop () = default Detailed Description Vulkan memory is exported as POSIX file descriptors ( BufferMemory::Shared ) and imported into the compute API as external memory; the compute driver is loaded at run time, so Ernie has no build dependency on any GPU toolkit. The two sides order their work on the GPU, without blocking the host, through two timeline semaphores created in Vulkan and imported into the compute API, one per direction so each side signals only its own: * compute to Vulkan: CopyToBuffer queues its copy and signals the next value; Vulkan submissions that read the buffer wait for VulkanWait . * Vulkan to compute: a Vulkan submission whose writes the compute side reads signals NextVulkanSignal ; compute streams wait for it with WaitForVulkan , and Download waits for it itself. Streams are numbered as in DLPack for the backend's device kind (for CUDA: 1 the legacy default stream, 2 the per-thread default stream, anything else a stream handle). Detailed Description Coordinates are the body-fixed frame: z towards the north pole and x towards longitude 0, in the same units as the radius. Each face is a grid of FaceCells() x FaceCells() quads whose FaceCells() + 1 squared vertices carry heights above the radius; vertex ( col , row ) of face f lies in direction FaceDirection(f, s, t) with s = 2 col / FaceCells() - 1 and t = 2 row / FaceCells() - 1. Vertices on an edge or corner of the cube appear on every face sharing it and must carry the same height there. Faces 0 to 3 straddle the equator, centred on longitudes 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees east, with columns running east and rows running south. Face 4 is centred on the north pole and face 5 on the south pole. On every face, column x row points into the body, so all faces wind the same way. Adjacent faces may run their grids in opposite directions along a shared edge. The projection is equiangular (Ronchi et al. 1996): s and t map to the face plane through tan(pi s / 4), so cells span nearly equal angles and areas differ by at most a factor of about 1.4 over a face, against 5.2 for a plain gnomonic cube. Grid lines are great circles. Select runs Strugar's algorithm on all six trees, using distances to each node's CubeSphereRegion . Neighbouring patches, across faces too, differ by at most one level when the first range is at least MinFirstRange . Odd vertices of a patch morph in 3D towards the midpoint of their two neighbours on the next coarser level: along the patch's edges these are the edge's own neighbours, and for vertices odd in both directions those on the quad diagonal from (1, 0) to (0, 1). Unlike the flat terrain's slide towards lower indices, this does not depend on which way a face's grid runs, so edges between faces match, and a fully morphed patch is exactly the coarser mesh. Positions on a planet need more precision than single floats. Selection works in doubles, and its frustum is relative to the eye: build it from a view-projection matrix whose view has the eye at the origin and the body frame's axes. References: * C. Ronchi, R. Iacono and P. S. Paolucci, "The 'Cubed Sphere': A New Method for the Solution of Partial Differential Equations in Spherical Geometry", Journal of Computational Physics 124(1):93-114, 1996. https://doi.org/10.1006/jcph.1996.0047 * F. The projection is equiangular (Ronchi et al. 1996): s and t map to the face plane through tan(pi s / 4), so cells span nearly equal angles and areas differ by at most a factor of about 1.4 over a face, against 5.2 for a plain gnomonic cube. Grid lines are great circles. Select runs Strugar's algorithm on all six trees, using distances to each node's CubeSphereRegion . Neighbouring patches, across faces too, differ by at most one level when the first range is at least MinFirstRange . Odd vertices of a patch morph in 3D towards the midpoint of their two neighbours on the next coarser level: along the patch's edges these are the edge's own neighbours, and for vertices odd in both directions those on the quad diagonal from (1, 0) to (0, 1). Unlike the flat terrain's slide towards lower indices, this does not depend on which way a face's grid runs, so edges between faces match, and a fully morphed patch is exactly the coarser mesh. Positions on a planet need more precision than single floats. Selection works in doubles, and its frustum is relative to the eye: build it from a view-projection matrix whose view has the eye at the origin and the body frame's axes. References: * C. Ronchi, R. Iacono and P. S. Paolucci, "The 'Cubed Sphere': A New Method for the Solution of Partial Differential Equations in Spherical Geometry", Journal of Computational Physics 124(1):93-114, 1996. https://doi.org/10.1006/jcph.1996.0047 * F. Strugar, "Continuous Distance-Dependent Level of Detail for Rendering Heightmaps", Journal of Graphics, GPU, and Game Tools 14(4):57-74, 2009. https://doi.org/10.1080/2151237X.2009.10129287

docs.text: The CUDA driver (libcuda) is loaded at run time, so Ernie has no build dependency on the CUDA toolkit; without an NVIDIA driver Create reports CUDA unavailable. CUDA work runs in the device's primary context, the one CUDA frameworks use, on the legacy default stream, so it is ordered after work that frameworks hand over through DLPack. Signals to Vulkan all go on the legacy stream, after an event recorded on the stream the work ran on, so values arrive in order however many streams write. Reference: NVIDIA, CUDA Driver API, "External Resource Interoperability", https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__EXTRES__INTEROP.html

docs.text: Class ernie::EditHistory ClassList > ernie > EditHistory Undo and redo for scene edits made through it: attribute sets and clears, prims defined, and prims removed with their descendants. More... #include <ernie/scene/edit_history.h> Public Functions Type Name void Add ( Scene & scene, const Scene & source, const Path & path) Copies the prim at path of source and its descendants, with their attributes and tensors (shared), to the same path of scene and records it; undoing removes them. void BeginGroup () Groups the edits until EndGroup into one step. Groups nest; the outermost counts. bool CanRedo () const bool CanUndo () const void Clear ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute) Clears attribute of the prim at path (back to its fallback) and records it. void Close () Ends the open step, so the next edit starts a new one. void Define ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view type) Defines the prim at path with type and records it; undoing removes it. void EndGroup () bool Redo ( Scene & scene) Redoes the last undone step (or group); returns whether there was one. std::string RedoLabel () const bool Remove ( Scene & scene, const Path & path) Removes the prim at path and its descendants and records them; undoing restores them, sharing their tensors. void Reset () Forgets every step, such as when the viewer switches scenes. void Set ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, Value value, bool open=false) Sets attribute of the prim at path to value and records it, dropping what was undone (the redo steps). void Set ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::vector< std::pair< std::string, Value > > edits, bool open=false) Sets several attributes of the prim at path , such as the transform ops of LocalTransformEdits , as one step. std::size_t Size () const The number of steps recorded, counting a group's edits one by one. bool Undo ( Scene & scene) Undoes the last step (or group); returns whether there was one. std::string UndoLabel () const A short description of the step Undo would undo, such as "/World/Cube xformOp:transform". Detailed Description Each records what it changes, so Undo puts it back (an attribute's earlier value, or none; a removed subtree with its attributes and tensors) and Redo does it again. Continuous edits, such as dragging a slider or a gizmo, merge into one step: an open edit of the same attribute as the last step updates that step until Close (called when the drag ends). Edits between BeginGroup and EndGroup , such as defining a prim and setting its attributes, undo and redo together. Edits made to the scene directly are not recorded; undoing past one sets the attribute to what the history last saw. Reference: E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson and J. Vlissides, "Design Patterns", the Command pattern, Addison-Wesley, 1994. More... #include <ernie/device/frame_uploads.h> Public Static Attributes Type Name constexpr std::uint32_t kSlots = 2 Frames that may be in flight at once. Public Functions Type Name void Begin (std::uint32_t slot) Starts staging into slot slot (below kSlots ), whose previous frame must have finished on the device. FrameUploads (const VulkanContext & context) VkDeviceSize Pending () const Bytes staged since the last Record . void Record (VkCommandBuffer commands) Records the staged copies, in order, between barriers: before, against every earlier command's access (including earlier submissions'), and after, making the copies visible to every later command. std::uint32_t Slot () const The slot of the last Begin . void Write (const GpuBuffer & destination, std::span< const std::byte > bytes, VkDeviceSize offset=0) Stages bytes for destination at offset ; the copy is recorded by the next Record , and dropped if destination is destroyed or replaced first. IsdCameraModel ( IsdSensor isd) glm::dvec3 LookAt (double time, double line, double sample) const The unit body-fixed direction of the ray at time through detector line line and sample sample ( IsdLineScanner::Look ). glm::dvec2 PixelOf (glm::dvec2 focal) const Image (line on the detector, sample) of distorted focal plane point focal . glm::dmat4 PoseAt (double time, const glm::dmat3 & axes) const The camera-to-body pose of Ernie's camera on axes at time . Protected Static Functions Type Name glm::dquat RotationAt (const IsdRotation & rotation, double time) The rotation rotation describes at time : its constant after its time-dependent part. Detailed Description Image coordinates are CSM's: (line, sample) with the first pixel's centre at (0.5, 0.5). The sensor's position is sampled as usgscsm samples it: at least 25 even times over the states, each a cubic Hermite of the states around it (ALE's spline) rotated into the body's frame, then interpolated eighth-order Lagrange (fewer points near the ends). Its orientation, sensor to body = body rotation x inverse pointing, is taken at the union of their times (each interpolated along the great arc), resampled evenly and interpolated the same way. Detector line d and sample s lie on the focal plane at the inverse of focal2pixel of (d x line summing + starting detector line - detector centre line, s x sample summing + starting detector sample - detector centre sample), in mm; the lens's distortion moves it; the camera looks along (-x, -y, -f) in the sensor's frame. Light-time and aberration corrections are left out, as usgscsm leaves them out. docs.text: Image coordinates are CSM's: (line, sample) with the first pixel's centre at (0.5, 0.5). The sensor's position is sampled as usgscsm samples it: at least 25 even times over the states, each a cubic Hermite of the states around it (ALE's spline) rotated into the body's frame, then interpolated eighth-order Lagrange (fewer points near the ends). Its orientation, sensor to body = body rotation x inverse pointing, is taken at the union of their times (each interpolated along the great arc), resampled evenly and interpolated the same way. Detector line d and sample s lie on the focal plane at the inverse of focal2pixel of (d x line summing + starting detector line - detector centre line, s x sample summing + starting detector sample - detector centre sample), in mm; the lens's distortion moves it; the camera looks along (-x, -y, -f) in the sensor's frame. Light-time and aberration corrections are left out, as usgscsm leaves them out.

docs.text: Struct ernie::LensModel ClassList > ernie > LensModel A lens: its projection, natural vignetting and transmission. More... #include <ernie/scene/camera.h> Public Attributes Type Name Spectrum chromaticFocusMm Axial colour ( ernie:lens:chromatic:focus ): the lens's focal length shift per wavelength in millimetres, the sensor staying at the reference's focus, which the defocus filter blurs each band by. Spectrum chromaticScale Lateral colour ( ernie:lens:chromatic:scale ): the image's scale per wavelength relative to the reference's, about the principal point, which the sensor resamples each band at. std::array< double, 4 > fisheye = {} Kannala-Brandt k1 to k4. double k1 = 0.0 double k2 = 0.0 double k3 = 0.0 double p1 = 0.0 double p2 = 0.0 LensProjection projection = LensProjection::Perspective std::shared_ptr< const LensRayTable > rays The lens's rays, in place of its projection and distortion when set ( ernie:lens:rays ): each sensor pixel sees along its interpolated ray, on cube faces past 60 degrees off axis. double transmission = 1.0 Fraction of light the optics pass. bool vignetting = false Natural falloff of irradiance off axis (cos^4 for pinholes). Public Static Attributes Type Name constexpr double kMaxFisheyeFieldAngle = 3.141592653589793 The largest field angle a fisheye may see, in radians (180 degrees off axis, a 360 degree field): one fisheye reaching past 60 degrees renders on cube faces ( wide_view.h ), which with the back face cover every ray. Public Functions Type Name glm::dvec2 Distort (glm::dvec2 undistorted) const Distorted normalised image coordinates of pinhole ones undistorted . double FieldAngle (glm::dvec2 distorted) const The field angle in radians of the ray landing at normalised image coordinates distorted . bool HasDistortion () const Whether Brown-Conrady distortion is set. bool IsPinhole () const Whether the lens is a pinhole: perspective without distortion. double NaturalVignetting (glm::dvec2 distorted) const The irradiance at normalised image coordinates distorted relative to the axis, from the aperture's foreshortening and the solid angle the image there sees: cos(theta) sin(theta) / (theta_d theta_d'), cos^4(theta) for a pinhole. glm::dvec2 Undistort (glm::dvec2 distorted) const The inverse of Distort : pinhole normalised image coordinates of the ray landing at distorted . Detailed Description A perspective lens has radial and tangential distortion (Brown-Conrady, in OpenCV's convention), which maps undistorted normalised image coordinates (x, y) = (X/Z, Y/Z) to distorted ones: x' = x (1 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4 + k3 r^6) + 2 p1 x y + p2 (r^2 + 2 x^2) y' = y (1 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4 + k3 r^6) + p1 (r^2 + 2 y^2) + 2 p2 x y A fisheye lens maps them to theta_d / r (x, y), with theta = atan(r) (OpenCV's fisheye model). The rasterizer draws a pinhole image and the sensor resamples it through the lens; a fisheye reaching past 60 degrees off axis is drawn on cube faces instead ( wide_view.h ), its field angle below kMaxFisheyeFieldAngle . docs.text: A perspective lens has radial and tangential distortion (Brown-Conrady, in OpenCV's convention), which maps undistorted normalised image coordinates (x, y) = (X/Z, Y/Z) to distorted ones: x' = x (1 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4 + k3 r^6) + 2 p1 x y + p2 (r^2 + 2 x^2) y' = y (1 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4 + k3 r^6) + p1 (r^2 + 2 y^2) + 2 p2 x y A fisheye lens maps them to theta_d / r (x, y), with theta = atan(r) (OpenCV's fisheye model). The rasterizer draws a pinhole image and the sensor resamples it through the lens; a fisheye reaching past 60 degrees off axis is drawn on cube faces instead ( wide_view.h ), its field angle below kMaxFisheyeFieldAngle . References: * D. C. Brown, "Decentering Distortion of Lenses", Photogrammetric Engineering 32(3):444-462, 1966. * J. Kannala and S. S. Brandt, "A Generic Camera Model and Calibration Method for Conventional, Wide-Angle, and Fish-Eye Lenses", IEEE TPAMI 28(8):1335-1340, 2006. https://doi.org/10.1109/TPAMI.2006.153 * OpenCV, "Camera Calibration and 3D Reconstruction", https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d9/d0c/group__calib3d.html , and "Fisheye camera model", https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/db/d58/group__calib3d__fisheye.html

Detailed Description A level-0 node spans leafCells x leafCells grid quads; a level-L node spans leafCells * 2^L and the single root node covers the whole raster. The tree stores only each node's min and max height, so selection can bound nodes in 3D for range and frustum tests. Select walks the tree from the root and picks, for each region, the coarsest level whose range covers it (Strugar 2009, algorithm 1). Every node is drawn as its four quarters, so all patches share one PatchCells() grid and differ only in origin and vertex spacing. Within each level's range the vertex shader morphs vertices towards the next coarser level, so switching level never pops; see terrain.slang . With a first range of at least MinFirstRange , neighbouring patches differ by at most one level and their shared edges match exactly, so no skirts or stitching are needed. References: * F. Strugar, "Continuous Distance-Dependent Level of Detail for Rendering Heightmaps", Journal of Graphics, GPU, and Game Tools 14(4):57-74, 2009. https://doi.org/10.1080/2151237X.2009.10129287 * P. Lindstrom, D. Koller, W. Ribarsky, L. F. Hodges, N. Faust and G. A. Public Static Attributes Type Name constexpr float kMaxPitch = 1.55f constexpr float kMinPitch = -1.55f Pitch stops short of straight down and up, where the view's up vector degenerates; views may look up from below the ground. Public Functions Type Name void Apply ( CameraParams & camera) const Sets camera 's transform, vertical field of view (through its aperture, keeping its focal length) and clipping range. glm::vec3 Eye () const Eye position in world coordinates. float FarPlane () const void Frame (const glm::vec3 & boundsMin, const glm::vec3 & boundsMax) Aims at the centre of the axis-aligned box [ boundsMin , boundsMax ] from a distance at which its bounding sphere fits the vertical field of view with a small margin. CameraParams MakeCamera (std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) const A default camera of width x height with this pose, field of view and clipping range. float NearPlane () const Clipping planes scaled to the orbit distance. void Orbit (float deltaYaw, float deltaPitch) Rotates by deltaYaw and deltaPitch radians, clamping pitch. void Pan (float dx, float dy, float viewportHeight) Moves the target parallel to the ground by a screen-space drag of ( dx , dy ) pixels in a viewport viewportHeight pixels tall, so the terrain follows the cursor at the target depth. void PanVertical (float dx, float dy, float viewportHeight) Moves the target across the screen by a drag of ( dx , dy ) pixels: sideways as Pan , and up and down along world z. glm::dmat4 Transform () const Camera-to-world transform of the eye looking at the target, +z up. void Zoom (float steps) Zooms by steps scroll steps; positive moves closer. Yaw rotates around the vertical axis (0 looks north, positive turns the view clockwise seen from above); pitch is the elevation angle of the eye above the target's horizontal plane. docs.text: Class ernie::RenderDelegate ClassList > ernie > RenderDelegate A render backend for a Scene , after Hydra's HdRenderDelegate: the rasterizer, and in future ray and path tracers, behind one interface that applications, the GUI viewer and the Python bindings drive without knowing which backend renders. More... #include <ernie/session/delegate.h> Public Functions Type Name virtual void AddSensorFilter ( SensorFilterModel model) = 0 Registers custom sensor filter model for SensorFilter prims to name in ernie:filter:type . virtual const BrdfRegistry & Brdfs () const = 0 The reflectance models materials may name in ernie:brdf . virtual ComputeInterop * Compute (std::string * why=nullptr) = 0 The compute interop (CUDA or HIP) of the delegate's device, connected on first use; null if unavailable, with the reason in why if given. virtual const RendererInfo & Info () const = 0 virtual Tensor MapArray ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, std::uintptr_t stream=1) Maps array attribute of the prim at path for writing in place on the compute device: syncs scene , writes into it as that attribute a tensor over the renderer's own memory for it, holding its values as they are, and returns that tensor. virtual Tensor MapArray ( Scene & scene, const PrimSet & prims, std::string_view attribute, std::uintptr_t stream=1) Maps array attribute written as rows of one array over prims ( Scene::Write of a PrimSet ), as the single prim's MapArray : writes the tensor as those rows, prim i's row i, and returns it. virtual std::optional< double > MeteredLuminance () const The scene's average luminance in cd/m^2 a recent frame measured with metering on ( tokens::kMeter ), for automatic exposure and meters; none before one has, or from backends that do not meter. virtual Path Pick (std::uint32_t x, std::uint32_t y) The prim the last frame Record drew shows at pixel ( x , y ) of its image, from its PrimId; the empty path for the background, a pixel outside the image, or a backend that cannot tell. virtual Path PrimPath (std::uint32_t id) const = 0 The prim path of a PrimId render var value, or the empty path for 0 or an unknown id. virtual void Record (VkCommandBuffer commands, const RenderingTarget & target, std::string_view var) = 0 Records the frame prepared by the last Update and draws its render var var (one of ViewVars ) into target.color (in the colour attachment layout, of the delegate's present format), as an image for display. Tensor Render (const Scene & scene, const Path & settings={}, Device device={}) Renders the first product of the settings and returns its LdrColor : a uint8 (rows, cols, 4) RGBA tensor, rows top to bottom, on the CPU, or with a GPU compute device (CUDA or ROCm) a linear tensor there that the GPU fills without the host. RenderDelegate (const RenderDelegate &) = delete virtual std::optional< Bounds3 > SceneBounds () const = 0 World bounds of what the delegate draws as of its last Sync or Update , for framing cameras; none if nothing has finite bounds (an infinite ground plane does not count). virtual const SensorFilterRegistry & SensorFilters () const = 0 The custom sensor filters registered so far. virtual void SetHighlight (std::span< const Path > paths, glm::vec4 colour) Outlines the prims at paths and their descendants in Record 's image, as Omniverse Kit outlines its selection, in display colour colour (sRGB-encoded rgb, alpha its opacity); none for no paths. virtual void SetViewBand (int band) Which spectral band Record shows when it presents SpectralRadiance: 0 to the camera's band count - 1, or -1 for the mean over the bands; backends that cannot choose ignore it. virtual void SetViewVar (std::string_view var) The render var the next Record draws, for Update to prepare the vars only drawing it needs (such as the opt-in MotionVector); call before Update . virtual RenderStats Stats () const = 0 RenderProductSetOutputs Step (const Scene & scene, std::span< const Path > products={}, const Path & settings={}) StepAsync(...).Fetch() . virtual StepOperation StepAsync (const Scene & scene, std::span< const Path > products={}, const Path & settings={}) = 0 Renders products of scene (see ResolveRenderProducts ) and returns at once: wait for or poll the operation, then fetch the outputs and map their render vars. virtual std::vector< TimelinePoint > SubmitWaits () const = 0 Semaphore waits the submission of commands from Record needs, for CUDA copies into the delegate's buffers that may still be running; empty without CUDA inputs. virtual void Sync (const Scene & scene) = 0 Uploads what changed in scene since the last call, or everything when scene is not the scene of the last call. virtual void Update (const Scene & scene, const Path & settings, VkExtent2D extent) = 0 Syncs, then prepares to draw the scene as the RenderSettings prim settings describes into an image of extent , for Record . virtual std::vector< std::string > ViewVars () const The render vars Record can draw of the frame the last Update prepared: Info() .viewVars and what that frame adds, such as the AOVs its sensor filters write ("aov:<name>"). RenderDelegate & operator= (const RenderDelegate &) = delete virtual ~RenderDelegate () = default Protected Functions Type Name FrameId NextFrame (const Scene & scene, const Path & settings, const Path & product) The frame of the next image of product (the settings' path for the interactive view): the ernie:frame of the resolved RenderSettings prim settings when authored, else how many images of the product this delegate rendered before; and the product's stream, StreamOf its path. RenderDelegate () = default Detailed Description The scene is the single source of truth. A delegate pulls its changes on Sync (each delegate keeps its own ChangeCursor ) and uploads only what changed, so there is no separate render index. Every backend reads the scene with the same resolution rules ( resolve.h ) and writes the same render vars through the camera's sensor filters ( sensor_filters.h ). There are two ways to render: * headless and in simulation: StepAsync (or Step and Render ) renders the UsdRender products of a scene and returns their render vars; * interactively: Update then Record into the application's own command buffer each frame, submitted after SubmitWaits . Rendering is deterministic: an image's noise and samples derive from the camera's ernie:sensor:seed , its render product's path and its frame number ( NextFrame ), so the same scene renders the same images on any machine and whatever else renders alongside. Public Functions Documentation function AddSensorFilter Registers custom sensor filter model for SensorFilter prims to name in ernie:filter:type . virtual void ernie::RenderDelegate::AddSensorFilter ( SensorFilterModel model ) = 0 Exception: std::invalid_argument if the model is invalid or fails to compile, or the backend runs no custom filters. function Brdfs The reflectance models materials may name in ernie:brdf . virtual const BrdfRegistry & ernie::RenderDelegate::Brdfs () const = 0 function Compute The compute interop (CUDA or HIP) of the delegate's device, connected on first use; null if unavailable, with the reason in why if given. virtual ComputeInterop * ernie::RenderDelegate::Compute ( std::string * why=nullptr ) = 0 function Info virtual const RendererInfo & ernie::RenderDelegate::Info () const = 0 function MapArray [1/2] Maps array attribute of the prim at path for writing in place on the compute device: syncs scene , writes into it as that attribute a tensor over the renderer's own memory for it, holding its values as they are, and returns that tensor. virtual Tensor ernie::RenderDelegate::MapArray ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, std::uintptr_t stream=1 ) Write into it on stream (which first waits for the frames already submitted), then scene.Unmap(path, attribute, stream) : the next frame draws the values without copying them.
